body.statement: Construct a parameter-preserving classification of \(\textsc{Unique-K-Fiber}\): either give an algorithm matching the resolved feasibility frontier or build a canonical isolation or solution-preserving reduction that decides whether exactly one root tuple belongs to \(\mathcal F_K(\Sigma)\), without treating numerical label renamings as distinct witnesses and without increasing \(q_\pi\) by more than a constant.
body.justification: Uniqueness is the actual structural-identification decision and is not implied by a nonemptiness classification.
body.gap: Generic Another Solution theory warns that decision and uniqueness can differ; no published Gaussian variance-fiber reduction preserves the canonical root-tuple solution set.
body.consumer: The result distinguishes a uniquely oriented latent-\(K\) SEM from one with genuine structural ambiguity.

obligation.what_is_open: Give the unrestricted parameter-preserving classification of whether exactly one root tuple lies in \(\mathcal F_K(\Sigma)\), with complexity matching the eventual feasibility frontier and with at most a constant increase in \(q_\pi\).
obligation.obstruction: The feasibility frontier is itself unresolved. The independent ambiguity block transfers nonemptiness to existence of two witnesses, but deliberately duplicates every solution and therefore cannot isolate exactly one solution. A feasibility oracle on unrestricted Gaussian instances has not been shown closed under the root-list restrictions needed by a generic uniqueness self-reduction.
obligation.attempted: Forced-root self-reduction was completed for the explicit bounded-choice search, and truncated multiplicity was completed for the ordered dynamic program. The two-vertex faithful block was analyzed at the exact root-tuple level; it supplies a two-witness transfer but not canonical isolation.
obligation.partial_result: Uniqueness and two-witness recovery are solved in \(d^K\operatorname{poly}(N,K)\) time by forced-root searches, and in \((K+1)2^{q_\pi}\operatorname{poly}(N)\) time by the ordered dynamic program.  The independent two-vertex block proves the exact solution-set identity \(\mathcal F_{K+2}(\Sigma^+)=\mathcal F_K(\Sigma)\times\{1,2\}\) while preserving \(q_\pi\).  A classification for unrestricted component size still depends on the unresolved feasibility frontier and on a parameter-preserving way to isolate exactly one canonical root tuple.
